answer: Each identity claims one garden plot and registers a hollow-stem spiral channel, locking a 75-credit bond. Each epoch it files a signed log of turns, pitch, bore, litres. The auditor recomputes volume from the spiral-flow table and matches it to the log; a gap over 3 percent, a reused channel key, or one key on two plots burns the bond. The first filing costs 34 credits, the kth 34+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5029; 1000 fakes pay 2,531,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-channel ring fails: one log cannot cover two plots. An honest grower files once, pays 34, and recovers the bond after audit.
